transcript: Season one solutions architect information, episode nine, LLM caching architecture. You can save 40% of your inferencing cost by implementing semantic caching. What exactly does semantic caching mean? Suppose if you are making a call, API call to an LLM with a particular query, the LLM receives the query, and it generates the response, and pushes the response to you to see what exactly the response for your query. And next time, in your organization, if another person comes and asks the same query, if that query is going to the LLM and it hits the LLM and gets the response again, it'll be a costly operation for you. Because the same duplicate query will be hit to the LLM two times, and your token cost will increase. So, in order to avoid this situation, you can build a semantic cache layer by using Redis and Qdrant vector DB database. So, this semantic layer acts as a caching mechanism. It caches the response produced by the LLM first time and stores in the cache. And when another person comes and asks the same question to the LLM, it does not go to LLM, but it retrieves the response from the cache and produces the response and sends the response to the user. This is called the caching architecture. As an AI enterprise architect, you must know this semantic caching mechanism when you implement AI agent project for your organization. All the best.
